title: Challenge is generated and passed to prove() but never verified against the assertion
description:
Found by the adversarial verifier during persona-okek, and left as a known limit of that change rather than fixed.

persona-grpc/src/service.rs generates 32 random bytes per request and hands them to prove(). Nothing ever compares the returned SignedAssertion against them. Claim::derive(candidate, evidence) is not given the challenge, so it structurally cannot check the binding, and the SignedAssertion is not carried into the Claim either.

ChallengeSignature::new is a public constructor taking arbitrary bytes, unlike VerifiedToken and HardwareTouch which have no public constructor. So an attestor inside this workspace can self-assert Possession and reach Iaa1 with no presence. Iaa2 and Iaa3 remain unreachable, which bounds the damage to the floor tier.

Why it was left: no attestor implements prove(), so no real signature exists to verify, and the public constructor is what keeps persona-grpc/tests/e2e.rs able to exercise the whole issuance and validation path with its five assertions intact. Closing it now would mean either deleting that coverage or building verification against a signature format nobody has written.

What closing it requires, for whoever implements the first real prove(): the challenge must reach the verifier alongside the assertion, the assertion must be checked against both the challenge and the candidate's key, and ChallengeSignature::new should then stop being public. Until then the honest statement is the one now in the code -- the binding is intended, not enforced.

The overclaiming comment at service.rs that said a proof is 'bound to this request' was corrected in 4698b8a.
